Open the API in a window with appropriate params and headers instead of using the Curl. User is navigated to Facebook login OAuth screen. On successful login, listen on window object for message where event listener returns data in its callback function. 
  ### Sample code to listen to event data:
    window.addEventListener('message', 
      function(e) {
        if (e.data && e.data.page === 'social_media_posting') {
        const { actionType, page, platform, placement, accountId, reconnectAccounts } = e.data
        }
      },
    false)
  ### Event Data Response:
    {
      actionType: string,            Ex: "close" 
      page: string,                  Ex: "social-media-posting" 
      platform: string,              Ex: "facebook" 
      placement: string,             Ex: "placement" 
      accountId: string,             Ex: "658a9b6833b91e0ecb8f3958" 
      reconnectAccounts: string[]]   Ex: ["658a9b6833b91e0ecb834acd", "efd2daa9b6833b91e0ecb8f3511"] 
    }
  ### The accountId retrieved from above data can be used to fetch Facebook account details using below API -
  API: '/social-media-posting/oauth/facebook/accounts/:accountId' 

  Method: GET

Returns more than the listing endpoint: Meta adds the fields relevant to the audience subtype (`retentionDays` and `customerFileSource` for customer lists, `rule` and `pixelId` for website audiences, `lookalikeSpec` for lookalikes), and this service appends `extras` describing the local smart-list or CSV source when the audience is a user-provided customer list.

Rename a Facebook custom audience or change its description. Only those two fields can be updated; membership is changed through the member endpoints. The audience is also queued for reprocessing, so the acknowledgement does not mean downstream state has caught up.

Retrieve Facebook custom audiences for a location. Without `limit` the response is a plain array. When `limit` is provided (max 100) the response is a paginated `{ customAudiences, paging }` envelope; pass `after` (from `paging.next`) to fetch the next batch. By default each item is returned in full; pass `projection` (comma-separated, dot-notation for nested fields, e.g. ?projection=id,name,dataSource.type) to return only the requested fields — any value outside the known field set is rejected.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size for a paginated fetch (max 100). When set, the response is a { customAudiences, paging } envelope instead of a plain array.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for the next batch, taken from the previous response paging.next

parameters.name: projection
parameters.description: Fields to return on each item, comma-separated (e.g. ?projection=id,name,dataSource.type). When set, only the requested fields are returned. Executes the specified agent and returns a non-streaming JSON response with the complete agent output. The agent must be in active status and belong to the specified location. locationId is required in the request body.

- For the first message in a new session, do not include the `executionId` in the request payload.

operations.summary: List the app templates a project can be created from.
operations.description:
The template catalog powers the template picker on the landing page:
the starters, then the vertical templates (ready-made vibe apps that
the Jenkins `vertical-templates-release` publishes). Each entry has a
stable `id`, a `category`, a human-readable `name` + `summary`, a
`version`, and the `stackTemplate` a project from it is created on.
A vertical template also names the CP Elements products it `uses`, and
its card picture when it has one (`previewUrl`). Pass the chosen `id`
as `templateId` and its `stackTemplate` on `createProject`.

operations.summary: Read an app's stack and open its sandbox for editing.
operations.description: Returns the app's stack, which decides how its code is written, and its kernel bundle, and opens the app's sandbox: read and edit it once `sandbox.status` is `ready`. A `react_native_app_kernel_v1` app is a phone app: its screens are files under `apps/mobile/app-extensions/`, registered with `POST .../sandbox/extension-routes`. Every other stack is a web portal.

operations.summary: Save the app's sandbox files as the point it restarts from.
operations.description: Saves the sandbox's files so a sandbox that restarts comes back with them. Call it after a set of `POST .../sandbox/edit` calls and before starting the run that builds them: a sandbox that restarts in between otherwise comes back with the files as they were at the last save.

reason.description: `turn_complete` after a set of edits (the default); `build_passed` after a build that passed.

operations.summary: Write or delete one file in the app's sandbox.
operations.description: Writes or deletes one file in the app's sandbox. After a set of edits, save them with `POST .../sandbox/checkpoint`, then start a run with `externalAgent: true` to check, build and deploy them. A React Native app (`react_native_app_kernel_v1`) writes only under `apps/mobile/app-extensions/` and `apps/mobile/application-assets/`; its `routes.ts` is generated, so register its screens with `POST .../sandbox/extension-routes` instead of writing that file.

path.description: File to write or delete, relative to the workspace root.

content.description: The file's full new content, encoded as `encoding` says.

operations.summary: Register, rename or remove a React Native app's screens.
operations.description: Changes the screen list of a React Native app (`react_native_app_kernel_v1`) once its screen files are written with `POST .../sandbox/edit`: `app-extensions/routes.ts` is generated from these changes, never written as text. Send several changes as one `batch`: all of them apply or none does, and a resent batch that is already in effect changes nothing (a repeated single `add` is refused as `duplicate_id`). The run started next with `externalAgent: true` checks the screens, saves them as a mobile revision and deploys the preview.

action.description: One change, or several as `{ "action": "batch", "changes": [...] }`. A change is `{ "action": "add", "route": { "id", "label", "icon", "requires"?, "parent"?, "copyKey"?, "filledIcon"? } }`, `{ "action": "rename", "id", "newId", "label"? }` or `{ "action": "remove", "id" }`. `id` is kebab-case and names the screen file; `icon` is one of the kernel's icon names, and an unknown one is refused; `parent` makes the screen a detail pushed from that route.

operations.summary: Search the app's code for literal text.
operations.description: Finds where text appears in the app's source files (ts, tsx, js, jsx, vue, json, md, css), with dependencies and build output left out. The text is matched literally, not as a pattern. Read the files it finds with `POST .../sandbox/view`.

query.description: The text to find, matched literally. It cannot start with '-'.

paths.description: Folders to search, relative to the workspace root; the whole app when absent.

items.description: A folder, relative to the workspace root, with no '..'.

maxResults.description: The most matching lines to return; 30 by default.

operations.summary: Read a file in the app's sandbox, or list a folder.
operations.description: Reads one file of the app's code, or lists a folder's files and subfolders, so an agent sees what is there before it edits. A folder path always lists. The kernel's own files are readable; the writable boundary applies only to `POST .../sandbox/edit`.

path.description: The file or folder, relative to the workspace root.

list.description: List the path even when it is a file's folder; a folder path lists either way.

operations.summary: Get an APK build's status and download link.
operations.description: Read it again until `status` is `finished`, when `artifactUrl` is a short-lived download link, or `failed`, when `error` says why.

parameters.name: apkBuildId
parameters.description: The build's id, from the response that started it.

operations.summary: Build a signed Android APK of a published phone app revision.
operations.description: Idempotent per Idempotency-Key. For a project whose current revision carries generated screens, the build is instead identified by the revision and the generated sources it carries (sha256(locationId:projectId:revision:sourcesSha)): repeating the request for the same revision and sources returns the same build whatever the key, and a failed one is queued again. Such a build is made from the React Native kernel commit the screens were generated against, and must be requested for the current revision. Generated screens reach members only through a new APK; they are never delivered over the air. At most one build may be active per project; sibling projects in the same location may build in parallel. Deleting a project while its build is still queued or building fails that build. A project compiles one signed APK for now: after a successful build the binary is final. A project without generated screens keeps reaching installed apps by publishing a revision; a project with generated screens cannot build another APK yet. Failed builds do not consume the allowance.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose for this build. Retrying with the same key returns the same build.

revision.description: The published revision to build. An app with generated screens builds its current revision.

operations.summary: Create a preview link token for a phone app.
operations.description: A short-lived token that makes the app's preview show this app. Open `sandbox.devUrl` from `GET .../cli/projects/{projectId}/context` with `#previewToken=<token>` appended; without it the preview shows the stock app.

expiresInSeconds.description: How long the preview link works, in seconds.

operations.summary: Publish a saved revision of an app to its members.
operations.description: For a phone app send `platform: mobile` and the `revision` from `GET .../app-config`: installed apps get it over the air. Screens your agent wrote reach members only in a new APK (`POST .../app-config/apk-builds`). `web`, the default, is for ClientPortal configuration apps; a coded web app publishes with `POST .../infra/promote-to-production`.

revision.description: The revision to publish: the app configuration's `revision`, once `appliedRevision` matches it and `status` is `ready`.

platform.description: `mobile` for a phone app. `web` (the default) publishes a ClientPortal configuration app's web revision.

operations.summary: Return a phone app to an earlier revision.
operations.description: Saves a copy of the earlier revision, screens included, as the newest one. Members get it once you publish it with `POST .../app-config/publish`.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The earlier revision to return to, from the app's revisions.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key you choose for this restore. Retrying with the same key returns the same restore instead of a second one.

baseRevision.description: The newest revision the caller saw (`revision` in the app's configuration). A save made since then refuses the restore instead of being overwritten.

operations.summary: List a phone app's saved revisions.
operations.description: Up to 50, newest first, marking the current one and the one members get. Return to one with `POST .../app-config/revisions/{revision}/restore`.

operations.summary: Get which revision of an app is newest, applied and published.
operations.description: A phone app saves a revision at the end of each run. Publish it with `POST .../app-config/publish` once `appliedRevision` equals `revision` and `status` is `ready`.

Idempotent on `planId`: a second (or concurrent) apply of the same plan
returns the first apply's result without writing again (`queued` while
the first is still running). Apply re-checks the stored change against
what exists now; when it moved, the answer is 409 `change_plan_stale`
with a fix (plan again). An expired plan is 409 too. A `partial` result
stays open: applying the same plan again finishes only what is left.
Another location's or project's plan is 404.

operations.summary: Check a change of one kind and sign a plan for it, without writing anything.
operations.description:
The caller's AI writes a `change` of one `kind`; the server validates it
against that kind's schema and against what exists now (CRM, modules,
saved customization) and answers what applying it would do. Nothing is
written and no model is called. `planId` is a signed token over
`{projectId, locationId, kind, changeHash}` that expires at `expiresAt`;
it is `null` when `ok` is false. The location is the session's, never
the body's. Kinds: `records`, `modules`, `appearance`, `mobile`,
`assets`, `domain`; any other kind is 400 `unsupported_change_kind`
naming the supported ones. `assets` plans also return `upload`: PUT the
image bytes to `upload.url` with `upload.headers`, then apply (apply is
409 `customizer_image_not_uploaded` until they land, and the plan stays
open). `domain` apply returns the DNS records to add in
`result.dnsRecords`; `GET /custom-domains` reports when it is active.

change.description: The change, in the shape GET /changes/schema gives for `kind`.

operations.summary: JSON Schema and an example for each change kind.
operations.description:
Static per server release: what `change` must look like for each kind
`POST /changes/plan` accepts, as JSON Schema (draft 2020-12, input
shape) with one valid example.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: One kind; absent returns every supported kind.

operations.summary: List the custom domains attached to a project.
operations.description: Lists the app's custom domains with their setup status and the DNS records to add. A domain is attached with `changes` kind `domain`; once it is `active` it serves the live site.

operations.summary: Publish an app to its live site.
operations.description: Publishes the app to its live site: its managed address, and every custom domain attached to it (`changes` kind `domain`) once that domain is `active`. A domain that becomes active later joins the live site without another publish. Check `GET .../publishability` first and send the `sourceRunId` it returns, so the build the creator approved is the one that goes live. Returns a publish job: poll `GET .../infra/publish-jobs/{publishJobId}` until `status` is `succeeded` (`publishedUrl` is the live site) or `failed` (`error` says why). Send the same `idempotencyKey` to retry safely.

sourceRunId.description: Exact successful run backing the preview approved by the creator. When provided, publish fails closed instead of selecting a different run that became ready concurrently.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable retry key. Domain-aware clients should always provide one; when omitted, source-bound requests receive a deterministic server-generated key while source-less legacy requests remain independent publish attempts.

operations.description: Reports a publish job's progress. Poll it every few seconds until `status` is `succeeded`, when `publishedUrl` is the live site, or `failed`, when `error` says why.

operations.summary: Check whether an app can be published now, and which build would go live.
operations.description:
Computed by the same resolver as promote-to-production. Without
`sourceRunId`: publishable iff some ready run of this project (caller's
location, main lineage) has a sealed build; the newest one goes live
with the newest config-only revision made on its lineage. With
`sourceRunId` (the reviewed preview): publishes what that preview shows —
its own sealed build, or for a ready run that built nothing, the sealed
build it descends from with config-only edits on that lineage; a run
that failed or has not finished is reviewed_preview_not_publishable. Send the returned
`sourceRunId` on promote-to-production. Tenant scope comes from the
session only.

parameters.name: sourceRunId
parameters.description: Run whose preview the creator is reviewing; bounds what may go live.

operations.summary: Answer every question of one form in a single write.
operations.description:
Records up to 12 answers in one run write and resumes the run once,
so a multi-question form does not resume the planner per answer.
Same per-answer rules as `POST …/answers` (records review approval
by `approve:<reviewId>` only, `decline:<reviewId>` declines,
anything else is a change request); `attachmentIds` are
ignored here. Project-scoped (`404` for another project's run);
`locationId` comes from the session, never from the body.

Idempotency: an answer whose `capId` and `correlationId` match the
recorded one is skipped; when every answer is such a duplicate
nothing is written and the run is not resumed again (still `202`).

answers.description: Each item is validated as `AnswerQuestionRequest`; `attachmentIds` are ignored on this route.

items.description:
One answer to a run question. No `locationId`: tenancy comes from the
session. For a records review `value` is `approve:<reviewId>`
(optionally `approve:<reviewId>:` + JSON with the `RoomChoice` keys
and/or `images`: `{"<change>:<fieldKey>": ["https://…"]}` for the
review's image columns) or `decline:<reviewId>`; anything else is a change request. For a
`RecordQuestionForm` `value` is the form's JSON.

capId.description: The question's id, e.g. `RunRecord.awaitingQuestion.capId` or a capability slug.

value.description: The answer: the chosen choice's label, the typed text, or the JSON a form asks for.

values.description: Every slug chosen for a multi-select question; `value` carries the same choices as labels.

comments.description: Anything the creator added to the answer.
comments.example: Members should see their progress first.

correlationId.description: Dedupe key; a repeat with the same `capId` and `correlationId` is a no-op.

attachmentIds.description: Reference images for the answer (single-answer route only).

items.title: AnswerQuestionRequest

operations.summary: Get the current state of a run (poll-friendly).
operations.description:
Strictly tenant- and project-scoped. A run that exists under a
different `projectId` (or under a different tenant entirely)
returns `404 not_found` — never `403`, never the run record.
This matches OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization
guidance: same shape for "doesn't exist" and "not yours".

operations.summary: List an app's runs, newest first.
operations.description:
Returns the project's runs ordered newest-first by `createdAt`. The
FE calls this when a user reopens a project to rebuild the chat
history; pair with `listAgentRunEvents` per run to replay each
prompt's full event log.

Production-backed by Mongo (`ai_builder_runs_records`). Persists
across pod restarts and is shared across pods.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Cap on the number of runs returned. Default 50. Pass `0` to
request every run (use sparingly — long-lived projects can
accumulate hundreds of follow-up runs).

operations.summary: Submit a prompt; the agent runs in the background.
operations.description:
Returns `runId` immediately. A sub-account token builds with its own agent: it writes the code
with `POST .../sandbox/edit` (and registers a React Native app's screens with
`POST .../sandbox/extension-routes`), saves the files with `POST .../sandbox/checkpoint`, then
starts the run with `externalAgent: true`, which checks, builds and deploys them. Poll
`GET .../runs/{runId}`: problems a passing build still has are in `checkProblems`.

The builder's own agent executes asynchronously:
attempt workspace restore from project's prior run → materialise
scaffold (only if no prior workspace) → loop tool calls → preflight
`pnpm build` → flush workspace to GCS → deploy via Cloud Build →
managed runtime revision replace → mark `ready` with a preview URL.

Per-project runtime services receive a stable public app hostname so the
iframe URL works without platform-session auth.

**Idempotency**: callers SHOULD send an `Idempotency-Key` header on
every retry. The server stores `(locationId, projectId, key)` →
`runId` for 24 h. Same key + same body → the original `runId` is
replayed. Same key + different body → `409 idempotency_conflict`.
Modeled after standard idempotent POST contracts; safe for browser
retries, network blips, and double-click submits.

**Attachment scope**: when `attachmentIds` are present, each id is
verified against the caller's tenant + project. Cross-project or
cross-tenant reuse is rejected with `403 attachment_not_owned`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Caller-generated key (UUID-v4 recommended) that makes this POST
safe to retry. Must match the prior request body byte-for-byte
on replay. Reused with a different body → `409`.

parameters.name: X-Correlation-Id
parameters.description:
Optional caller-supplied trace id. When omitted, the API mints
`cid_<uuid>` and echoes it back via the response
`X-Correlation-Id` header. Threaded through audit rows + logs.

prompt.example: Add a page listing upcoming events

displayText.description:
What the creator's chat bubble shows for this run instead of
`prompt`, when the client sends an instruction the creator did not
type (for example a suggestion chip, whose full text carries
verifier output or a planner directive for the agent). One plain
line. Omitted for typed messages, whose bubble is the prompt.

productTarget.description: What the project builds; the project's own by default.
productTarget.title: ProductTarget

customCode.description:
ClientPortal-only per-run switch. When false or omitted, the agent
can inspect the project and apply SDUI configuration, but source-code,
shell, dependency, and build tools are unavailable. When true, the
existing full custom-code tool surface is enabled. This choice does
not change sandbox provisioning or preview lifecycle behavior.

clientPortalSurface.description:
ClientPortal-only context captured from the selected builder surface.
Unqualified follow-ups default to this lane; explicit web, mobile,
or web-and-mobile wording in the prompt takes precedence.

externalAgent.description:
An agent outside the builder (an MCP client) writes this run's code in
the project's sandbox. The run skips the builder's agent: a first build
asks the builder's intake questions (answered through the answers
API), then every run checks, delivers, registers the sandbox with
ClientPortal, and seals a publishable release.

mobilePipeline.description:
Deprecated compatibility field for older mobile clients. New mobile
runs use the standard builder flow with the React Native app kernel.

mobilePipelineSpeed.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. Accepted for older mobile clients but
no longer selects a distinct generation pipeline; production mobile
codegen uses the single-loop Mastra path.

modelId.description:
Model id from `GET /api/v1/catalog/models`. When provided, this
single model is used for every phase of the agent (classify,
plan, code). When omitted, the platform routes to its per-phase
defaults (Haiku → Sonnet → Opus).

agentId.description:
Optional id of a user-defined agent profile created via
`POST /api/v1/agents`. The profile's `systemInstructions` and
`skills` are appended to the platform's catalog for this run,
and its `defaultModelId` is honoured when `modelId` is not set.

mode.description:
Run mode. The composer's 3-way segmented control surfaces:

  - `auto` (default) — agent honours the classifier's
    `recommended_mode` and decides whether to plan, ask, or
    build straight through.
  - `plan`           — agent always proposes a plan first via
    `propose_plan` and pauses for approval. The plan is
    surfaced as a `plan_approval_request` narrator event;
    the user POSTs an approve/refine/reject verdict to
    `/agent-runs/{runId}/plan-approval`.
  - `build`          — agent skips planning and goes straight
    to file_editor (only `ask_user` when the classifier
    flags a high-cost architectural unknown).
  - `plan_first`     — back-compat alias for `plan`. v1
    callers still emit it; the runtime treats it as `plan`.

attachmentIds.description:
Optional ids of attachments previously created via
`POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/attachments/upload-url`.
Surfaced to the agent as user-provided context so generated
code can reference uploaded files (logos, PDFs, brand assets).

selectedElements.description:
Visual edits (vibe apps): the elements the creator selected in the
live preview before sending. The agent receives them as a
`<selected-elements>` block after the prompt, so "this" means the
element on screen. Context only: file and line are hints the agent
checks against the workspace.

elementType.description: Lower-case tag name of the element, e.g. `h1`.

filePath.description: Where the element is written, relative to the app root (no `..` segment, not absolute; Nuxt route characters such as `[id]` and `(group)` allowed).

ownerFilePath.description: The page that renders the design-system component this element is the root of. Same rule as `filePath`.

textContent.description: The element's visible text, with emails and phone numbers redacted by the preview.

attrs.description: A small set of the element's HTML attributes (id, role, type, name, links without their query, aria-*…).

operations.description: Returns one app: its status, publication state, preview and production URLs, and its latest run.

operations.summary: Rename an app, archive it, or pin it to the top of the app list.
operations.description: Renames the app, archives it or brings it back, or pins it to the top of the app list. Send only the fields to change.

archived.description: Archive the app, or bring it back; an archived app is hidden from the app list.

starred.description: Pin the app to the top of the app list.

operations.summary: List projects in the caller's location.
operations.description: Lists the ClientPortal apps in the sub-account, most recently active first. A sub-account token sees every app by default; `view=mine` limits the list to apps the caller created.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
Ownership scope within the authenticated caller's location.
`mine` returns only projects owned by the caller and requires
`projects:read`; `all` returns every project in the location and
requires `projects:read_all`. The location is always taken from
the authenticated session and cannot be overridden.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Exact project-status filter. When omitted, all statuses except
`deleted` are returned. Results remain scoped by `view` and the
authenticated caller's location.

operations.description: Creates an app in the sub-account. Then start its first build with `POST .../agent-runs`; a sub-account token sends `externalAgent: true` because its own agent writes the code.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to retry: a repeat with the same key returns the first result.

additionalPhones.description:
Add additional phone numbers to a contact. > ⚠️ **Important:** When sending `additionalPhones`, you must also include the contact’s current primary `phone` in the same request.
If you send `additionalPhones` without `phone`, the contact’s existing primary phone may be cleared or replaced.
  • phone represents the contact’s primary phone number.
  • additionalPhones represents secondary phone numbers for the same contact.
  • Always send the primary phone together with additionalPhones when updating phone numbers.
  • A maximum of 10 additional phone numbers can be provided.
  • phoneLabel is optional. Allowed values: Home, Work, Mobile, or Landline. A label can belong to only one phone number on the contact, including the primary. If a label is repeated, it is kept on the first phone number and removed from the others.
Example ```json { "phone": "+14155550100", "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Avoid ```json { "additionalPhones": [ { "phone": "+14155550101", "phoneLabel": "Work" } ] } ``` Sending only `additionalPhones` may cause the existing primary phone number to be lost. If phone uniqueness is enabled for the location, every phone number in the request—primary and additional—must be unique across contacts. If any phone number already belongs to another contact, the request fails with **400 Bad Request** and no changes are saved.

operations.description:
Get Duplicate Contact.

If `Allow Duplicate Contact` is disabled under Settings, the global unique identifier will be used for searching the contact. If the setting is enabled, first priority for search is `email` and the second priority will be `phone`.
Search contacts based on combinations of advanced filters. Documentation Link - https://doc.clickup.com/8631005/d/h/87cpx-158396/6e629989abe7fad

The Upsert API will adhere to the configuration defined under the "Allow Duplicate Contact" setting at the Location level. If the setting is configured to check both Email and Phone, the API will attempt to identify an existing contact based on the priority sequence specified in the setting, and will create or update the contact accordingly.

If two separate contacts already exist—one with the same email and another with the same phone—and an upsert request includes both the email and phone, the API will update the contact that matches the first field in the configured sequence, and ignore the second field to prevent duplication.

operations.description: Post the messageId for the API to delete a scheduled email message.

Update delivery events, per-recipient statuses, and the overall message status for an email sent via a custom conversation provider.

### Authorization
- Requires the `conversations/message.write` OAuth scope.
- The calling OAuth app must own the conversation provider that originally sent the email.
- Attempts to update emails sent via LC Email or Mailgun will return `403 Forbidden`.

### Updatable Fields
All request body fields are optional. Pass only what you need to update.

**`events`** — Aggregate delivery event counters (integers). Counters are merged into the existing values (not replaced). Setting a counter to `0` is treated as no-op and will **not** reset the stored value.

**`recipients`** — Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a `MessageStatus` value. Use `failReason` to capture bounce or rejection details when the status is `failed`.

**`status`** — The overall message status. Accepts any `MessageStatus` enum value.

### Event Inference
The API automatically infers related events to maintain data consistency:
- **`clicked`, `complained`, `unsubscribed`, or `replied`** → implies `opened` (set to 1 if not already provided and open tracking is enabled) and `delivered` (set to 1).
- **`opened`** → implies `delivered` (set to 1 if not provided).
- **`delivered`, `permanent_fail`, or `temporary_fail`** → implies `accepted` (set to 1 if not provided).

### Timestamps
The API automatically records server-side timestamps on first occurrence for `delivered`, `opened`, and `clicked` events. Subsequent updates to these counters do not overwrite the original timestamp.

schema.description:
Request body to update the delivery status of an email message. `status` is required. `events` and `recipients` are optional and may be included together with `status`.

- Use `events` to report aggregate delivery metrics (delivered count, open count, etc.).
- Use `recipients` to track per-recipient delivery outcomes for multi-recipient emails.
- Use `status` to set the overall message status.

Multiple calls are additive — event counters are merged, recipient statuses are upserted, and the message status is overwritten.

events.description: Aggregate delivery event counters. Counters are merged into existing values. The API automatically infers related events (e.g., reporting `clicked` will also set `opened` and `delivered` if not already present). See the endpoint description for the full inference rules.

allOf.description: Aggregate delivery event counters for the email message. Values are merged into existing stored counters (additive update, not replacement). A value of `0` is treated as a no-op and will not reset the stored counter. Only include fields you want to update. Provider-specific counters such as `permanent_fail`, `temporary_fail`, and `esp_isp_block` may be sent using those snake_case keys.

additionalProperties.description: Additional provider event counter (merged into stored values).

delivered.description: Number of successful deliveries — the recipient mail server accepted the message. Automatically inferred (set to 1) when `opened`, `clicked`, `complained`, `unsubscribed`, or `replied` events are reported.

opened.description: Number of unique open events (typically tracked via a tracking pixel). Automatically inferred (set to 1) when `clicked`, `complained`, `unsubscribed`, or `replied` events are reported, provided open tracking is enabled on the email.

clicked.description: Number of link click events within the email body. Triggers automatic inference of both `opened` and `delivered`.

replied.description: Number of reply events. Triggers automatic inference of both `opened` (if open tracking is enabled) and `delivered`.

failed.description: Total number of delivery failures (includes both permanent and temporary). For more granular failure tracking, use `permanent_fail` and `temporary_fail` instead.

accepted.description: Number of messages accepted by the receiving mail server for delivery. Automatically inferred (set to 1) when `delivered`, `permanent_fail`, or `temporary_fail` events are reported.

rejected.description: Number of messages rejected outright by the receiving mail server (before acceptance).

unsubscribed.description: Number of unsubscribe events triggered by the recipient. Triggers automatic inference of `opened` and `delivered`.

complained.description: Number of spam complaint events (e.g., recipient marked the email as spam). Triggers automatic inference of `opened` and `delivered`.

stored.description: Number of messages stored by the email service provider (ESP-specific event).

allOf.title: EmailEventsDto

recipients.description: Per-recipient delivery statuses. Each entry maps a recipient email address to a delivery status. Entries are upserted — if a recipient already has a status, it will be overwritten with the new value.

items.description: Delivery status for an individual recipient of a multi-recipient email. Each entry is keyed by the recipient's email address and tracks their specific delivery outcome independently from the aggregate event counters.

emailId.description: The recipient's email address. This is used as the key to store and update the per-recipient status. Must match one of the original recipients of the email.

status.description: The delivery status for this specific recipient. Common values for status updates: `delivered` (successfully delivered), `failed` (delivery failed — provide `failReason`), `opened` (recipient opened the email), `clicked` (recipient clicked a link).

failReason.description: Human-readable reason for the delivery failure. Only applicable when `status` is `failed`. Examples: "Mailbox not found", "Quota exceeded", "Blocked by recipient server".

items.title: UpdateRecipientMessageStatusDto

status.description: The overall status of the email message. Required on every request. For emails with multiple recipients, consider using the `recipients` array for granular tracking and this field for the aggregate status.

operations.description: Get email by Id

Export messages for a specific location with cursor-based pagination support.

**Channel Filtering Behavior:**
- **When channel is omitted:** Returns all non-email message types, including messages that don't belong to any specific channel.
- **When channel=Email:** Returns email messages only.
- **When channel is specified (SMS, Call, WhatsApp, etc.):** Returns messages for that specific channel.

**Limitations:**
- Group Chat and SMS Review Request message types are not supported.
- Activity messages (opportunity updates, appointments, etc.) are not included in the export. Use `GET /conversations/{conversationId}/messages` (Get messages by conversation id) to fetch them.
- Cursor validity is 2 minutes from the last request made.

operations.description:
Post the necessary fields for the API to upload files. The files need to be a buffer with the key "fileAttachment".

Note: One of conversationId or contactId must be provided.

File Size Limits:
  • Maximum file size: 5 MB
  • Maximum files per upload: 5

Allowed file types:

Images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, HEIC, AI

Videos: MP4, MPEG, 3GP

Audio: MP3, WAV, WAVE, AIFF, AIF, AIFC, GSM, ULAW, OGG, AAC, M4A, AMR

Documents: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ODT

Archives: ZIP, RAR

Other: VCF, VCARD (contact files), ICS (calendar files)

The API will return an object with the URLs

Secure attachments: Set isSecureAttachment to true to upload the file as a secure attachment. This is currently supported for the email channel only; support for the remaining conversation channels is coming.

A secure attachment is returned with a /files/d/{slug} URL that is publicly accessible for one hour after upload. After that window the attachment becomes private — to render, download, or retry access, extract the {slug} from the returned URL and call GET /files/d/{slug} with a bearer token carrying the files.readonly OAuth scope, which returns a short-lived signed download URL. A file uploaded without this flag keeps its existing permanently accessible URL.

Note: From 30 November 2026 every file uploaded through this endpoint is stored as a secure attachment, and the isSecureAttachment field is ignored.

A secure attachment URL is publicly accessible for one hour after upload, after which the file must be fetched with GET /files/d/{slug} using the files.readonly OAuth scope. operations.description:
Post the necessary fields for the API to upload files. The files need to be a buffer with the key "< custom_field_id >_< file_id >".
Here custom field id is the ID of your custom field and file id is a randomly generated id (or uuid)
There is support for multiple file uploads as well. Have multiple fields in the format mentioned.
File size is limited to 50 MB.

The allowed file types are:
  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • DOC
  • JPG
  • JPEG
  • PNG
  • GIF
  • CSV
  • XLSX
  • XLS
  • MP4
  • MPEG
  • ZIP
  • RAR
  • TXT
  • SVG


The API will return the updated contact object.

operations.description:
Updates the name and/or description of an existing knowledge base.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the knowledge base to update

name.description: field to update the name of the knowledge base

description.description: field to update the description of the knowledge base
description.example: An updated description for this knowledge base

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a knowledge base and its associated trained content.
WHEN TO USE: use this when the whole knowledge source is no longer needed; use deleteTrainedUrlsForKnowledgeBase or delete (FAQ) to remove only some content.
RETURNS: whether the delete succeeded.

parameters.name: knowledgeBaseId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the knowledge base to delete

operations.description:
Retrieves one knowledge base by id, including name, metadata, and timestamps.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to inspect a single knowledge base; use listAllKnowledgeBasesPaginated to browse; use updateKnowledgeBase to rename it.
RETURNS: success and the knowledge base record.

parameters.name: knowledgeBaseId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the knowledge base

operations.description:
Returns a paginated, searchable list of sitemap URLs without starting a crawl.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to preview sitemap URLs before a crawl; use discoverWebsite to start discovery; use trainDiscoveredUrls after pages are found.
RETURNS: a paginated list of sitemap URLs.

url.description: Website URL to preview sitemap for

operations.summary: Get crawling status for the latest operation
operations.description:
Fetches crawl/train progress for a specific operation, or the latest operation when operationId is omitted.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to poll a discoverWebsite or trainDiscoveredUrls run; do not use it to start a crawl or train pages.
RETURNS: aggregated counts by status plus detailed operation information.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: operation id as string (optional - gets latest if not provided)

operations.summary: Train discovered website pages and ingest into the knowledge base
operations.description:
Queues selected discovered pages so the AI ingests their content into the knowledge base.
WHEN TO USE: use this when discoverWebsite has already found pages; use discoverWebsite to crawl first; use deleteTrainedUrlsForKnowledgeBase to untrain pages.
RETURNS: whether training was queued, a status message, and the URL ids that were accepted.

urlIds.description: List of URL IDs to train

operations.description:
Removes trained website pages from a knowledge base so the AI no longer references them.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to drop specific or all trained URLs; use trainDiscoveredUrls to add pages; use getAllWebsiteUrlsDataByKnowledgeBase to list what is trained.
RETURNS: whether the delete succeeded.

excludeUrlIds.description: URL IDs to exclude from a deleteAll operation (select-all-minus-some flow)

search.description: Substring filter (case-insensitive) matched against `url` or `title` to scope deleteAll to filtered rows only. Mirrors the search semantics of the list endpoint.

operations.summary: Get all trained page links by knowledge base
operations.description:
Lists discovered and trained website pages for a knowledge base, with pagination and optional URL filter.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to inspect crawled pages; use discoverWebsite to find new pages; use deleteTrainedUrlsForKnowledgeBase to remove pages the AI should stop using.
RETURNS: a paginated list of crawled URLs with status, title, and identifiers.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: query to filter on url links

operations.summary: Start crawling and discover pages for training
operations.description:
Starts a website crawl that discovers pages for later AI training.
WHEN TO USE: use this when you need to scan a site before training; use trainDiscoveredUrls to ingest selected pages; use getCrawlingStatusForLatestOperation to poll progress.
RETURNS: the discovery operation id, current status, and the URL being crawled.

url.description: Website URL as string

preSelectedUrls.description: Pre-selected URLs from sitemap preview — when provided, only these URLs are crawled

autoTrain.description: Automatically train the discovered URLs after crawling

operations.summary: Delete an existing knowledge base FAQ

operations.summary: Update an existing knowledge base FAQ

Task fields: `status`, `assignees`, `parentTaskId`, `dueDate`, `startDate`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `contactId`, `businessId`, plus custom-field keys. Unknown field or operator is rejected by search (422). Groups may nest. Do not combine `listIds` with a `graph` filter.

field.description: Field to filter. Task properties use their public names (`status`, `dueDate`, `assignees`, …). Record timestamps: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.

operator.description: Comparison operator. `exists` / `not_exists` take no value. List scope uses `nested` on field `graph` (see Search Tasks). Date ranges use `gte`/`lte` or `range`. Allowed: `eq`, `not_eq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `contains_set`, `range`, `nested`, `exists`, `not_exists`.

value.description: Comparison value. Omitted for `exists` / `not_exists`. Arrays for `contains_set`. Nested filters when `operator` is `nested`.

additionalProperties.description: Value for one custom field. Type depends on the field definition (string, number, boolean, array, or null). Discover keys via the Custom Fields API with `objectKey: "task"`.

group.description: How child filters combine. Allowed: `AND`, `OR`. Groups may nest up to 3 levels deep.

filters.description: Child filters or nested groups (max nesting depth 3).

listIds.description: List ids to scope the search (max 10). Equivalent to one nested `graph` filter (`type=list`, `id` eq or `contains_set`). More than 10 ids, a non-list target, or a second graph scope returns **422** (`error`: `graph_scope_invalid`).

field.description: Field to sort by. Allowed: `dueDate`, `startDate`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. These tie-break safely with the `[sortValue, taskId]` searchAfter tuple.

subtaskViewMode.description: How subtasks appear. Allowed: `collapsed` (parents only), `expanded` (parents with embedded `subtasks[]`), `separate` (subtasks as their own records with `parentTaskId` / `parentName`). Requires a Tasks V2 / Kanban location. On any other location this field, or a `parentTaskId` filter, returns **422**. `parentName` and `subtasks` are search-only — Get Task By ID, Get Tasks, and Fetch Tasks By IDs do not populate them. `total` is the hit count after filters and access scope (post-RBAC). Page with `searchAfter` until it is null.
