operations.description:
Remove a like from a comment by its internal comment ID (the `_id` returned by the list-comments endpoint — not the native platform ID).

Works for any comment level — top-level comments, replies, and replies-to-replies. **Supported platforms:** Facebook, LinkedIn, Community, TikTok, Bluesky. Instagram is not supported (passing `instagram` returns 400).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Platform that supports liking / unliking comments (Instagram is not supported)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Internal comment ID — the `_id` returned by the list-comments endpoint (`POST /comments/{platform}/list`). Not the native platform comment ID. Works for any comment level: top-level comments, replies, and replies-to-replies.

operations.description:
Like a comment by its internal comment ID (the `_id` returned by the list-comments endpoint — not the native platform ID).

Works for any comment level — top-level comments, replies, and replies-to-replies. **Supported platforms:** Facebook, LinkedIn, Community, TikTok, Bluesky. Instagram is not supported (passing `instagram` returns 400).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Platform that supports liking / unliking comments (Instagram is not supported)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Internal comment ID — the `_id` returned by the list-comments endpoint (`POST /comments/{platform}/list`). Not the native platform comment ID. Works for any comment level: top-level comments, replies, and replies-to-replies.

operations.summary: List comments for a post or thread
operations.description: Paginated list of comments scoped to a post (`parentId` = postId) or a comment thread (`parentId` = commentId). Use `skip`/`limit` for pagination, `sortBy` for ordering, `originIds` to filter by connected account, and `search` for keyword search.

fromDate.description: Start of the published-date window (ISO 8601). If provided, `toDate` is also required, and `fromDate` must be ≤ `toDate`. Omit both to disable date filtering.

toDate.description: End of the published-date window (ISO 8601). If provided, `fromDate` is also required.

originIds.description: Origin IDs of connected accounts to filter by

sortBy.description: Sort by top comments or latest comments

skip.description: Pagination offset — number of comments to skip (zero-based). Must be ≥ 0.

limit.description: Pagination page size — number of comments to return. Must be between 1 and 100.

parentId.description: Parent ID — pass the internal post ID (for replies under a specific post) or the internal comment ID (for replies under a specific comment). Omit to list all top-level comments for the location filtered by `originIds`. Must be a valid 24-character internal ID, not the native platform ID.

operations.description:
Create a top-level comment on a post (`isParentThread: true`, `parentId` = postId) or a reply to an existing comment (`isParentThread: false`, `parentId` = commentId). Per-platform content max length: Facebook 8000, Instagram 2200, Linkedin 3000, Community 8000, Tiktok 150, Bluesky 300, Youtube 10000, Threads 500.

**Optional-field platform support:**
- `attachments` — supported on **Facebook only**. Ignored on Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Bluesky, Community (Community processes the field but external URLs are not rendered due to its bucket restriction).
- `mentions` — supported on **Facebook**, **LinkedIn**, and **Community** only. Ignored on Instagram, TikTok, Bluesky.
- `notifyAllGroupMembers` — supported on **Community** only. When `true`, all group members get a push/in-app notification (equivalent to an `@everyone` broadcast). Independent of the `mentions` array and of `@everyone` text in `content`. Default `false`.

parentId.description: For top-level comments (`isParentThread: true`): pass the post ID returned by the posts API. For replies (`isParentThread: false`): pass the parent comment ID returned by the list-comments API. In both cases this must be a valid 24-character internal ID — not the native platform ID.

isParentThread.description: Set `true` to create a top-level comment on a post (parentId = post ID). Set `false` to create a reply to an existing comment (parentId = comment ID).

content.description: Content of the comment. Per-platform max length: Facebook 8000, Instagram 2200, Linkedin 3000, Community 8000, Tiktok 150, Bluesky 300, Youtube 10000, Threads 500.

attachments.description: Attachments for the comment (max 1 image). **Supported on:** Facebook only. **Not supported on:** Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, Bluesky, Community — the field is accepted by the API but the attachment will not appear on the comment. (Community processes the field server-side, but external URLs are not rendered due to its bucket restriction.)

url.description: URL of the attachment

mentions.description:
Mentions for the comment. **Supported on:** Facebook, LinkedIn, Community. **Ignored on:** Instagram, TikTok, Bluesky — the field is accepted but mentions are not rendered on these platforms.

`offset`/`length` must locate `name` inside `content` exactly — `content.substring(offset, offset + length) === name` — otherwise the request is rejected with 400. The example below aligns with the `content` example above.

name.description: Mention name. Must appear verbatim in `content` at `offset`.

id.description: Mention ID

offset.description: Zero-based character index in `content` where `name` starts. For content `"Great post, Alex Morgan!"` the mention `"Alex Morgan"` starts at 12.

length.description: Character length of `name` — `content.substring(offset, offset + length)` must equal `name`.

slug.description: Mention slug for community profile link

notifyAllGroupMembers.description:
When `true`, all members of the Community group receive a push/in-app notification about this comment — equivalent to an `@everyone` broadcast.

**Supported on:** Community only. Ignored on all other platforms (the field is accepted but no notification is sent).

**Independent of the `mentions` array** — you do not need to add an `@everyone` entry to `mentions` for this to take effect. Conversely, putting the literal text `@everyone` in `content` does **not** by itself trigger notifications; only this flag does.

Defaults to `false` (no broadcast notification). Use `true` only when the comment is genuinely intended for every member of the group — overuse may cause members to mute the group.

pollOptions.description: Poll options for Threads reply (2-4 options)

textAttachment.description: Text attachment for Threads reply with optional styling info

threadLocationId.description: Location ID for Threads reply location tagging

operations.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 2: Get Available Accounts

After completing OAuth authentication (Step 1), use this endpoint to retrieve the list of available pages, channels, or locations that can be connected.

### OAuth Flow Position

1. **Start OAuth** → User authenticates, returns `accountId`
2. **Get Accounts** (this endpoint) → Lists available pages/channels to connect
3. **Attach Account** → Connect the selected account

### What This Returns

The response varies by platform:

| Platform | Returns |
|----------|--------|
| **facebook** | List of Facebook Pages the user manages |
| **instagram** | List of Instagram Professional Accounts (linked to Facebook Pages) |
| **google** | Google Business Profile locations |
| **linkedin** | LinkedIn Pages and Profile |
| **tiktok** | TikTok Creator account info |
| **tiktok-business** | TikTok Business Center accounts |
| **youtube** | YouTube Channels |
| **pinterest** | Pinterest Business accounts and boards |
| **threads** | Threads profiles |

### Next Step

From the response, select the account/page you want to connect and use its details in Step 3:
```
POST /social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
```

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Social media platform. Must match the platform used in the preceding steps of the OAuth flow.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: The Location ID where you want to connect this social account

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The OAuth Account ID received from Step 1 (Start OAuth) via the window message event

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search term to filter accounts/pages by name. Useful when the user has many pages to choose from.

operations.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 3: Connect the Account

This is the final step in the OAuth flow. After retrieving available accounts (Step 2), use this endpoint to connect the selected account to your location.

### OAuth Flow Summary

1. **Start OAuth** → User authenticates with platform
2. **Get Accounts** → Retrieved available pages/channels
3. **Attach Account** (this endpoint) → Connect the selected account

### Request Body

The accepted fields depend on the `platform` path parameter — pick the matching schema in the request body below. Most platforms take the `originId`, `name` and optional `avatar` of the account you selected in Step 2; Google Business Profile takes the full `location` and `account` objects.

> `tiktok-business` accounts are connected through the TikTok Business flow, not this endpoint.

### After Connection

Once connected, the account will appear in your location's connected accounts and can be used for social media posting.

operations.description:
## OAuth Connection Flow - Step 1: Initiate OAuth

This is the first step in the 3-step OAuth flow to connect a social media account:

1. **Start OAuth** (this endpoint) → User authenticates with the platform
2. **Get Accounts** → Retrieve available pages/channels to connect
3. **Attach Account** → Connect the selected account to your location

### How to Use

Open this API in a browser window (not via cURL) with the required query parameters. The user will be redirected to the platform's OAuth login screen.

### Receiving the OAuth Response

After successful authentication, the OAuth window will post a message back to your application. Listen for this message to get the `accountId` needed for the next step.

```javascript
window.addEventListener('message', function(e) {
  if (e.data && e.data.page === 'social_media_posting') {
    const { actionType, page, platform, placement, accountId, reconnectAccounts } = e.data;
    // Use accountId for Step 2: GET /oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
  }
}, false);
```

### Event Data Response

| Field | Type | Example | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| actionType | string | "close" | The action type |
| page | string | "social-media-posting" | Source page identifier |
| platform | string | "facebook" | The OAuth platform |
| placement | string | "placement" | Placement context |
| accountId | string | "658a9b6833b91e0ecb8f3958" | **Use this for Step 2** |
| reconnectAccounts | string[] | ["658a9b...", "efd2da..."] | Accounts that need reconnection |

### Next Step

Use the `accountId` from the response to call:
```
GET /social-media-posting/oauth/{locationId}/{platform}/accounts/{accountId}
```

### Platform Notes

- **bluesky**: Currently not supported, will return an error
- **tiktok-business**: Uses a separate business OAuth flow

- **youtube**: YouTube Channels
- **pinterest**: Pinterest Business Accounts
- **threads**: Threads Profiles
- **bluesky**: Bluesky Accounts (currently not supported)

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Replace a workflow definition in full. **This is a complete overwrite** — any step absent from the request is deleted, so always read the current definition first and send it back modified — the definition carries its own `version`, so sending back what you read keeps you protected against overwriting a concurrent edit. A stale `version` is rejected with 422 and nothing is written.

**Draft only.** A published workflow is rejected with 409: the overwrite would replace steps under contacts currently moving through it. Set the workflow to draft with Update Workflow Status, update it, then publish it again.

**Order matters.** Changing status advances the `version`, so read the definition *after* setting the workflow to draft: draft → read → update → publish. Reading first and drafting second leaves you holding a stale `version`.

version.description:
The workflow's version counter, owned by the system — not a format version. Get Workflow Definition fills it in; leave it untouched and send it back on update, and a concurrent edit in the builder can never be silently overwritten. A stale value is rejected with 422.

Treat it as opaque: echo it, never compute from it. It does not always advance by one (delete and restore each add 0.1, and a later save rounds up), so it is not always an integer.

Required on update: send back the value you read. An update without it is rejected with 422 before anything is written.

linear.description:
The smallest useful workflow: a trigger, two actions, and one edge joining them. `edges` is what orders the steps — `actions` is an unordered set, so a definition with no edges is a pile of disconnected steps, not a sequence.

Note `tags`: tag names are matched against the sub-account. A name that does not exist yet comes back as a warning (`ASSET_TAG_NOT_FOUND`), the step is saved as written, and the tag is created the first time the step runs. Other references — users, pipelines, calendars, custom fields, templates — must already exist, or the save is rejected.

branching.summary: 2. If/else — two lanes from one condition
branching.description:
A branch is an `if_else` action that declares its `branches`, plus one edge per branch whose `branch` is that branch's `id`. Give each branch a UUID `id`. The else lane is created for you and named by `noneBranchName`; reach it with an edge whose `branch` is `no`. A declared branch with no edge returns a warning, because contacts matching it would stop there.

Send `version: 2` on the step. `conditionName`, `operator`, `if`, `noneBranchName` and `branches` are required, and every condition needs `conditionType`, `conditionSubType` and `conditionOperator`, plus `conditionValue` unless the operator takes none, as `has_value` here does not. A branch without a complete condition is rejected with 422. For other fields and operators, build the condition once in the builder and read it back with Get Workflow Definition.

wait.summary: 3. Wait — pause before the next step
wait.description:
A `wait` is an ordinary action on the path, not a property of its neighbours. This one holds the contact for two days before the follow-up.

`startAfter.type` accepts `seconds`, `minutes`, `hour`, `hours` or `days`, and `when` is `before`, `after` or `now`. Business-hours behaviour goes in `settings.window` at the root — not on the wait step.

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Count the log records of one workflow, grouped by one or more dimensions. It answers how many: enrollments, completions, failures per step, why contacts left, and trends over time. To answer who, use Get Workflow Logs.

**Before you call it.** Get `workflowId` from Search Workflows. Never pass a workflow name.

**Grouping.** Each row holds one value for every dimension in `groupBy`, plus `count`. Grouping by `week`, `day` or `hour` adds `bucket`, the start of each interval in `timezone`. `startDate` and `endDate` always stay UTC. Rows are sorted by the grouped values in ascending order (`status`, then `type`, `stepId`, `removedReason` and `bucket`), not by count.

**Finding filter values.** Group by a dimension to see which values this workflow has, then filter on them. For example, `groupBy=removedReason` lists the reasons present, and those values work in `removedReasons`.

**Steps.** Rows grouped by `stepId` also carry `stepName`, the name of that step on its most recent log record in the date range. `stepId` matches `actions[].id` in Get Workflow Definition. A step count includes the `remove_from_workflow` record written when a contact leaves the workflow at that step, so group by `stepId` and `type` together to count how often the step itself ran.

**Common questions.**
- Enrollments: `statuses=added_to_workflow`
- Completions: `removedReasons=end_of_workflow`. Divide by enrollments for a completion rate
- Failures per step: `statuses=error,failed,failed_retry_limit_reached&groupBy=stepId`
- Why contacts left: `types=remove_from_workflow&groupBy=removedReason`
- Stopped because the contact replied: `removedReasons=contact_reply_stop_response`
- Goal reached: `types=workflow_goal&statuses=success`
- Enrollment trend: `statuses=added_to_workflow&groupBy=week` (or `day`)
- Change over time: cal

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Sub-account (location) ID. It must be the sub-account the token belongs to, otherwise the request is refused with 403

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the range, ISO 8601: a plain date (start of that day, UTC) or a full timestamp. Send it together with endDate. Defaults to 30 days ago. Logs are available for the last 60 days, so it cannot be earlier than that

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the range, ISO 8601. A plain date includes the whole day. At most 30 days after startDate. Defaults to now

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: Dimensions to group the counts by. Repeat the parameter or send a comma-separated list. `status` is the step outcome, `type` the step type, `stepId` the step, `removedReason` why the contact left the workflow, and `week`, `day` or `hour` a time bucket (one at most). Defaults to `status`

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Count only these step outcomes. Values: `added_to_workflow` (the contact entered the workflow), `success` (the step ran), `error` and `failed` (the step did not complete), `failed_retry_limit_reached` (the step gave up after its retries), `retry` (the step will run again), `skipped` (the step did not run, for example because of DND, a time window or missing data), `waiting` (the contact is waiting at the step), `wait_finished` (a wait ended), `finished` (the contact left the workflow, see removedReason), `paused_due_to_draft_mode` (the workflow was unpublished while the contact was in it), `contact_merged` (the contact was merged into another contact), `drip_queued` (the contact is waiting in a drip step for its batch), `drip_resume` (the batch was released and the contact moved on), `processing` (the step has started and has not finished yet), and `winner_declared` (an A/B test step picked its winning path; the record has no contact). New values can appear. Group by `status` first to see the values this workflow has

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Count only these step types: a step `type` key, as listed by Get Step Types or in `actions[].type` of Get Workflow Definition. Unlike Get Workflow Logs, `if_else` and `drip` match only those exact keys here. New values can appear. Group by `type` first to see the types this workflow has

parameters.name: removedReasons
parameters.description: Count only records removed for these reasons. Values: `end_of_workflow` (the contact reached the end), `contact_deleted` (the contact was deleted), `deleted_workflow` (the workflow was deleted), `record_deleted` (the record was deleted), `goal_action` (a goal step removed the contact), `contact_reply_stop_response` (the contact replied and the workflow stops on reply), `contact_merge` (the contact was merged), `appointment-change`, `invoice-change` and `service-booking-change` (the appointment, invoice or booking changed and the workflow restarted for the contact), `attendee-change` (the Events attendee or their event changed, and the run for that attendee ended), `rental-booking-change` (the rental booking that started the workflow was deleted or cancelled), `wait_step_window_in_past` (a wait step time window pointed to a time in the past, so the contact left), and `missing-data` (the step the contact was on was deleted from the workflow). Values are exact, including the ones with hyphens. New values can appear. Group by `removedReason` first to see the values this workflow has

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA timezone for the week, day and hour buckets. It does not move startDate and endDate, which stay UTC. Defaults to UTC

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of grouped rows. A grouping that produces more is refused with 422 rather than truncated. Default 1000, maximum 5000

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

List the step-by-step execution history of one workflow, newest first. Each record is one step of one run for one contact or record, with its outcome and timing. It answers who and what: who entered, what happened to a contact, which steps failed and for whom. To answer how many, use Get Workflow Log Statistics.

**Before you call it.** Get `workflowId` from Search Workflows. Never pass a workflow name. To see what each step is, call Get Workflow Definition: its `actions[].id` matches `stepId` here.

**Step details.** `meta` says how the contact entered, why a step was skipped or failed, what a step did, whether a wait timed out, and why the contact left. A key is left out when it does not apply. Only the keys documented under `meta` are returned. New keys may be added later (see Compatibility).

**Paging.** The response holds `logs`, their `count`, and `nextCursor`. The first call (`action=first`, the default) returns the newest page. For the next (older) page, send `action=next` with `referenceId` and `referenceCreatedAt` from `nextCursor`, unchanged, and keep the same filters and dates. `nextCursor` is null when there are no more records. A cursor that does not match returns 422. A page holds at most 100 records, 15 by default.

**Dates.** Send `startDate` and `endDate` together (ISO 8601, UTC, at most 30 days apart). Without them, the last 30 days are returned. Logs are available for the last 60 days.

**Common questions.**
- Who entered the workflow: `statuses=added_to_workflow`
- Which steps failed, and for whom: `statuses=error,failed,failed_retry_limit_reached`
- What happened to one contact: `contactId=<contact ID>`
- Every step of one run: `executionId=<workflowStatusId of any record from that run>`

An empty `logs` list is a real answer: nothing matched in that window. A `workflowId` t

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Create a workflow from a complete definition. The definition is validated in full before anything is persisted, so a rejected request creates nothing. Workflows are always created in `draft`; use Update Workflow Status to publish.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Sub-account (location) ID the workflow belongs to

system.description: Identifier for the system authoring this definition

workflowId.description: Your own identifier for the workflow, echoed back for correlation

triggers.description: Triggers that enrol contacts. May be empty — a workflow with no trigger can still be entered by another workflow or by the API — but the key must be present.

name.description: Display name shown on the canvas

conditions.description: Trigger filters. Shape depends on `type`; use Validate Workflow Definition to check it.

scheduleConfig.description: Schedule for scheduler-type triggers. Absent on every other trigger type. Get Workflow Definition returns it in this shape and Update Workflow Definition accepts it back.

stopAt.description: When the schedule stops firing, as epoch milliseconds (UTC). Omit for no end date.

skipWeekends.description: Skip runs that would fall on a Saturday or Sunday.

id.description: Trigger ID. Assigned when omitted. Get Workflow Definition returns it; sending it back keeps the trigger stable across updates.

position.description: Canvas position, as the builder stores it. Echoed by Get Workflow Definition; optional on write.

testResponse.description: Sample event captured by the builder for testing the trigger. Passed through verbatim.

workflowsTriggerType.description: Marketplace (IATF) triggers only: the trigger class the app registered. Echoed by Get Workflow Definition; send it back unchanged.

integrationAccountId.description: Marketplace (IATF) triggers only: the connected account the trigger listens on.

masterType.description: Trigger family, as the builder stores it.

targetActionId.description: For triggers bound to one step (a reply trigger, for example), the ID of that step.

triggerRelation.description: How multiple triggers combine. Echoed by Get Workflow Definition; ignored on write — the system always stores `or`.

actions.description: Steps. May be an empty array, but the key must be present.

id.description:
Step ID. Any non-empty string, unique within the definition — a readable id like `welcome-sms` is fine, and `edges` reference it by that name. It does not have to be a UUID; ids that are not get converted to one when the workflow is saved, so a definition read back will carry the converted ids rather than the ones sent.

**Reuse ids across updates.** A step keeps contacts already mid-workflow on their current step only while it keeps its id. Sending back the ids from Get Workflow Definition is the reliable way to do that — a readable id also converts to the same value every time for a given workflow, so re-sending an authored definition is safe too.

name.description: Display name shown on the canvas

attributes.description: Step configuration. The shape depends on `type` — fetch it from Get Step Types and check it with Validate Workflow Definition.

position.description: Canvas position, as the builder stores it. Echoed by Get Workflow Definition; optional on write.

workflowsActionType.description: Marketplace (IATF) steps only: the action class the app registered. Echoed by Get Workflow Definition; send it back unchanged.

isMarketplaceAction.description: Marketplace (IATF) steps only: marks the step as a marketplace action.

container.description: ID of the container step this step is nested in, where the builder uses one.

edges.description: Connections between steps. May be empty, but the key must be present.

from.description: Step ID this edge leaves from

to.description: Step ID this edge arrives at

branch.description: Branch label, for steps that fan out. On an if/else it is the `id` of one of the step's declared `branches`, or `no` for the else lane.

goto.description: Marks this edge as a loop back to an earlier step

allowReEntry.description: Allow a contact to enter the workflow more than once

stopOnResponse.description: Stop the workflow when the contact replies

days.description: Days of week the window applies to, 0 = Sunday

senderAddress.description: Default sender details, passed through verbatim. Recognised keys are `from_name`, `from_email` and `from_number`. Declared as a free-form object rather than a typed schema because those keys are snake_case on the wire — the workflow format uses them verbatim, and a typed schema would fail the public-spec camelCase rule while renaming them would break round-tripping.

folderName.description: Single-segment folder to place the workflow in. Mutually exclusive with `folderPath`.

folderPath.description: Folder path, outermost first, max 10 levels. Mutually exclusive with `folderName`.

createFolderIfMissing.description: Create the folder if it does not exist. Requires `folderName` or `folderPath`.

version.description:
The workflow's version counter, owned by the system — not a format version. Get Workflow Definition fills it in; leave it untouched and send it back on update, and a concurrent edit in the builder can never be silently overwritten. A stale value is rejected with 422.

Treat it as opaque: echo it, never compute from it. It does not always advance by one (delete and restore each add 0.1, and a later save rounds up), so it is not always an integer.

Omit it on create — the system assigns the starting value.

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Find workflows in a sub-account by name, status, folder or timestamp. Returns summaries only — pass an ID to Get Workflow Definition for the full definition.

Filters are combined with AND. Page with `offset` for the first few pages and switch to the `searchAfter` cursor for deeper paging; sending both is rejected.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Sub-account (location) ID the workflow belongs to

filters.description:
Filters, combined with AND. Max 20. Omit to match every workflow in the sub-account.

To fetch a known set of workflows, filter `workflowId` with `in`. The sub-account scope still applies, so an id from another sub-account simply matches nothing.

operator.description: Comparison to apply. `eq`, `not_eq`, `in`, `contains` and `not_contains` are text-only; `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` are date-only. A mismatch is rejected with 422. To match a single instant on a date field, send `gte` and `lte` with the same value.

value.description: Value to compare against. An array is required for `in` and rejected for every other operator. Dates are ISO-8601.

sort.description: Sort order. Defaults to most recently updated first.

offset.description: Result offset. Cannot be combined with `searchAfter`. Deep paging is expensive — prefer `searchAfter` past the first few pages.

searchAfter.description: Cursor from a previous response, for stable paging through a large result set. Send it back verbatim; do not construct one.

byName.description: Workflows whose name contains `onboarding`, most recently updated first. With no `offset` or `searchAfter` the first page comes back, and the response carries the `searchAfter` cursor for the next one.

nextPage.summary: 2. Next page — cursor from the previous response
nextPage.description: The same filters and sort, plus the `searchAfter` the previous page returned, sent back verbatim. Do not send `offset` with it: the two are rejected together.

publishedByIds.description: `in` takes an array and is the way to fetch a known set of workflows. Filters are combined with AND, so the `status` filter narrows that set to the ones that are live.

operations.description:
**Limited availability.** The workflow API is currently enabled for selected sub-accounts only; any other sub-account receives 403 `WORKFLOW_API_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_LOCATION`.

Browse or fetch the action and trigger schemas available to a sub-account, so a definition can be built against real field names before saving.

Every response is paged and every entry carries its full field schema, including the `assetReferences` that say which fields must hold IDs of assets that already exist. Default page size is 20.

Narrow with `types`, which matches on the step type **key** and matches partially — `email` returns `send_email` as well as `email`. Use `query` instead to match names and descriptions too. Page with `limit` and `skip`.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Sub-account (location) ID the workflow belongs to

parameters.name: types
parameters.description:
Comma-separated step type filters (max 50 terms). Each term matches any step type whose **key** contains it, so `email` returns `send_email` as well as `email`, and an exact key still matches itself. Matching looks only at the type key — not the name or description — so a step merely described as emailing something will not appear.

A term matching nothing is reported in `notFound`. Results are paged like any other request.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Restrict results to actions or triggers

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free-text match over type, name and description — broader than `types`, which matches the type key only. Ignored when `types` is supplied.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Kept small by default because every entry carries its full field schema.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of results to skip before the page starts
